revised_comments: Access to electricity in Guinea shows a stark urban-rural divide. World Bank data for 2023 puts urban access at 92.5% of the urban population against just 25.7% in rural areas, a gap of 66.8 percentage points. World Bank programme documents for Guinea's National Least-Cost Electricity Access Program (NLCEAP, 2022-2027) corroborate this pattern, citing roughly 89% urban versus 21% rural grid access, with national access reaching 53% by end-2024 against an NLCEAP target of 55% by 2027. The gap remains well above 60 percentage points.
